title: RAW_UNREVIEWED: visible repair versus deliberate joined/split contrast at f75v.44
summary: GDT850 records one definite split `qol chedy` and one joined `qolchedy` in the same f75v.44 line; GDT852 independently observes a localized physical seam contrast. A separate source hypothesis is that the later joined occurrence is a visible writing repair or compressed echo of the earlier `chedy qol` tandem, rather than a stable semantic alternation. Inspect only the already admitted native f75v line for erasure, overwrite, ink interruption and local crowding, with same-line ordinary joins as controls. Clean, uncorrected ductus would defeat the specific visible-repair version, though silent copying error and deliberate semantic contrast would remain open.

design.mechanism: A local writing repair or echo produces the joined surface after the repeated split construction.
design.unit: Previously admitted f75v.44 native line and preselected same-line spacing controls, with GDT850/851 exact group positions fixed.
design.contrast: Visible repair or compressed echo versus an uncorrected intentional spacing distinction.
design.prediction: The joined second site shows a predeclared correction trace, altered ink continuity, or exceptional local crowding relative to surrounding group joins; clean ordinary strokes and spacing reject the visible-repair model. Neither outcome translates qol or chedy.
design.scope: Exploratory source audit only; f75v already admitted, no reserve access; GDT852's seam finding is retained, not rerun.
